name: Upper blepharoplasty
lead: Upper blepharoplasty is surgery on the upper eyelids that removes or repositions excess skin, orbicularis oculi muscle and sometimes fat [1][2][3]. People choose it to make the eyes look more open, rested and defined: hooded or heavy lids that crowd the lash line and shorten the visible eye are lifted away, the lid crease becomes visible, and the upper eyelid contour reads more clearly [3][21]. The incision is placed in the natural eyelid crease so the scar is concealed [3].

It is performed for functional reasons, such as excess skin (dermatochalasis) that obstructs the upper visual field, and for cosmetic reasons, such as hooded or tired-looking lids [4][29]. It is often described as one of the most common aesthetic procedures in the United States [22], and Wikipedia describes blepharoplasty as the second most popular cosmetic procedure worldwide, after botulinum toxin injections [28]. The term blepharoplasty was coined in 1818, and an excision to relax the eyelids appears in a first-century Roman medical text [3]. The operation is often combined with brow lifting or ptosis repair [5][6][20].

In looksmaxxing discussion, the eye area is treated as a central part of facial impression, and hooded upper lids are one of the features people talk about changing. Surgeons writing in the literature make a parallel point: one review describes the periorbital region as central to facial appearance and says a motivated patient can improve appearance beyond simple age reversal [21]. Forum members who have had eyelid surgery post before-and-after photos and recovery reports [30].

Published research includes surgical technique papers, randomised trials comparing wound closure, anaesthesia and muscle-removal approaches [7][23][24][25][26], a 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis of techniques [16], a 2014 evidence-based review [8], and studies of how the lid and brow shape perceived tiredness and how rejuvenation surgery changes perceived attractiveness [9][18]. Registered trials are studying outcomes such as dry eye, vision quality and patient-reported satisfaction [10][11][12].

paras: In appearance terms, upper blepharoplasty is aimed at hooded eyes. Skin that droops over the lashes can hide the lid crease and make the eyes look smaller or tired; removing it exposes more of the eye and gives a cleaner lid line [4][21]. Fat prolapse and asymmetry between the two lids can be addressed in the same operation [4]. A 2008 perception study using digitally altered photographs found that pretarsal lid height and the crease were the main drivers of how tired a face looked, which is the visual territory this operation works on [18].

Functional indications include dermatochalasis that impairs peripheral vision and is documented by visual field testing, which supports insurance coverage in some systems [4]. Wikipedia describes dermatochalasis as an excess of eyelid skin that can hang over the lid margin and, in severe cases, obstruct a large part of the superior visual field; it typically becomes more noticeable from around age 40 and affects men and women equally [29]. Wikipedia also notes it can contribute to tension-type headaches because the forehead muscles work to hold the lids up [29].

Cosmetic indications include hooded lids, fat prolapse and asymmetry, aimed at a more rested or youthful appearance [4]. Contributions from brow ptosis are sometimes addressed at the same time, since patients can compensate by overworking the frontalis muscle [4][19]. The American Society of Plastic Surgeons describes eyelid surgery as treating loose upper-lid skin that creates folds or changes eyelid contour, and, in some cases, impairs vision [15].

The Roman author Aulus Cornelius Celsus described an excision of skin to relax the eyelids in De Medicina in the first century, according to Wikipedia [3]. Karl Ferdinand von Gräfe coined the word blepharoplasty in 1818, when the technique was used to repair eyelid deformities left by cancer [3].

Later work added combined approaches. A transcoronal eyebrow lift with concomitant upper blepharoplasty was described in 1983, using the brow arch familiar to makeup artists as a marking guide [5]. Limited-incision forehead lifts (1996), subperiosteal brow lifts and transpalpebral work on the corrugator and procerus muscles followed as ways to improve upper-lid results [6][13][14]. A 1999 randomised study compared tissue glue with sutures for closing the incision [7]. Reviews in 2002 and 2004 mark a shift from excision of skin, muscle and fat toward more conservative, volume-conscious approaches, because older methods could leave a hollowed, operated look [2][1].
Double-eyelid surgery has become very popular in East Asia, particularly South Korea and Taiwan, where Wikipedia describes it as among the most common aesthetic procedures [3][28].

A skin ellipse is marked and removed along the crease, with orbicularis muscle and herniated fat removed or preserved depending on the surgeon's plan [1][4]. Reviews describe a move from excision-only operations toward conservative, volume-preserving and rejuvenative approaches that consider the brow and the wider periorbita [1][2]. One review says a good crease allows surgeons to focus on lid contouring with less skin and fat excision, and that careful lipofilling can restore the softness of younger eyes [21].

Variants described in the literature include skin-only excision, skin with muscle excision, skin with fat removal or fat preservation, and combinations with brow elevation by transcoronal, limited-incision, subperiosteal or browpexy routes [5][6][13][20]. A review of surgery in older patients describes usually creating a double fold and leaving the lower skin flap unstretched to avoid an aggressive look [19]. Corrugator and procerus resection through the lid incision has also been reported [14]. Closure may use sutures or tissue adhesive [7][34]. Wikipedia notes that CO2 laser is used by some surgeons as an alternative to a scalpel and that there is debate whether that counts as surgery [3].

Eyelid crease shape and fat distribution differ between populations. Wikipedia reports that double-eyelid prevalence varies widely between East Asian studies, and that Asian eyelids have been reported to carry more fat than White eyelids in a 1999 study; the single-versus-double crease trait is polygenic [28]. Surgery in people with a low or absent crease is often aimed at creating a crease rather than only removing skin [3][4]. A 2013 review of surgery in older patients says surgeons may or may not create a double eyelid fold and discuss pros and cons with the patient [19].

The epicanthic fold often accompanies a single eyelid and is sometimes addressed with epicanthoplasty at the same time [28]. See the separate entry on non-incisional double eyelid suture for the suture-based alternative, and Wikipedia's note that tape or glue is widely used to simulate a crease without surgery [28].

Reviews say assessment typically includes a medical and ophthalmic history, a vision examination, and evaluation of brow position, existing ptosis, lower-lid position and cheek projection [22]. Pre-existing dry-eye symptoms are described as correlating with postoperative problems, so they are asked about [22]. Preoperative screening also commonly covers thyroid eye disease, bleeding disorders and body dysmorphic disorder [4].

Brow position matters because many people with heavy lids raise the brow to compensate. A 2012 study of 60 East Asian patients (120 eyes) measured the distance between lid margin and brow six months after upper blepharoplasty or levator advancement and found it shortened after both, with larger changes after levator advancement; the authors recommend telling patients beforehand that brow position may change [17]. A 2023 randomised trial of 54 patients likewise reported lower eyebrow height after surgery with either technique [25].

Operations are usually outpatient and take about one to three hours [3]. Swelling and bruising are common and generally resolve over several weeks; cold compresses and head elevation are often recommended, and sutures may be removed within several days or be absorbable [3]. A forum poster who posted results two weeks after surgery described remaining swelling while noting a visible difference, and listed neck training, brow thickening and tanning as further steps in their plan [30].

A randomised trial of 68 patients compared a sharp needle with a blunt microcannula for the anaesthetic injection and found mean pain scores of about 2.85 and 2.50 out of 10, a difference that was not statistically significant, with similar bruising [26]. Another randomised double-blind trial of tranexamic acid with epinephrine and lidocaine examined intraoperative bleeding and postoperative inflammation [27].

The evidence-based review in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery says upper-lid complications are uncommon with current techniques, in contrast to lower-lid surgery, which carries potentially more serious complications [8]. The 2023 systematic review of 20 studies found few complications and generally satisfied patients [16]. Surgeons' reviews include sections on recognising and treating postoperative complications, and describe pre-existing dry eye and changes in brow position as issues to discuss with patients [1][22][17]. Wikipedia notes that excess lid skin and surgery both sit close to the eye and that care is needed [28].
Dry eye and changes in vision quality after upper blepharoplasty are subjects of several registered studies [11][12][35].

Evidence consists of case series, technique papers and a modest number of randomised trials. A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis searched PubMed, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov and CENTRAL, included 20 studies (nine in the meta-analysis) across six surgical types, and examined intraocular pressure, corneal measures, visual acuity, tear tests and dry-eye questionnaires; the meta-analysis found no significant differences and few complications were reported [16].

A pair of double-blind randomised trials in 54 patients each compared skin-only upper blepharoplasty with skin plus muscle removal. FACE-Q patient-reported scores rose over 12 months in both groups with most domains similar, though the eyes-in-general score was higher in the skin-only group at 12 months, and scarring did not differ [24]. In the companion tear-film trial, subjective irritation and vision-related symptoms improved after either technique, while objective tear measures were unchanged at 12 months [23]. In the headache trial, patients reported fewer headaches and lower eyebrow height after surgery with no difference between techniques [25].

A prospective, randomised, blinded study of 20 patients compared octyl-2-cyanoacrylate tissue glue with sutures for upper blepharoplasty closure [7]. A 2015 retrospective study rated photographs of 30 women before and after facial rejuvenation surgery, including blepharoplasty among other procedures, and found significant gains in rated attractiveness, femininity, likeability and social skills; it was not a study of blepharoplasty alone [9].

Registered trials include studies of vision quality [11], functional changes [35], muscle versus fat removal and dry eye [12][31], medial fat pad preservation [32], a small-incision fat-removal technique [36], a comparison with a newer device-based lift [33], and patient-reported outcomes with the FACE-Q instrument [10].

Wikipedia reports that women accounted for about 85 percent of blepharoplasty procedures in the US in 2014 and about 88 percent in the UK [3]. It also reports a cost range of roughly 2,000 to 4,000 US dollars for double-eyelid surgery, flagged there as needing a citation, and that many people travel to South Korea for the procedure [3]. Wikipedia describes social pressure on women in some East Asian settings to have the surgery or to use taping alternatives [28].

On looksmaxxing forums, users compare eyelid surgery with other approaches to the eye area, and post results threads for procedures such as ptosis repair and upper-lid surgery; commenters in one thread debated whether the posted images showed natural or posed results [30]. Non-surgical alternatives for lid shape, such as the non-incisional double eyelid suture, have their own entry.

lore.intro: Upper eyelid surgery comes up in looksmaxxing spaces as a way to change hooded eyes, usually in results threads where members post photos and recovery notes [30]. Surgeons' literature frames the same operation in terms of function, rejuvenation and brow position.

claims.claim: Removing hooded skin makes the eyes look bigger and more open.
claims.believers: Posters who have had upper-lid surgery report a visible difference in the eye area even while swollen [30].
claims.experts: Surgical reviews describe the operation as exposing the lid crease and lash line, and a 2008 perception study tied lid height and crease to perceived tiredness [21][18].

claims.claim: The result is a one-time permanent fix.
claims.believers: Some forum members treat eyelid surgery as a finished step on the way to being 'maxxed' [30].
claims.experts: Dermatochalasis is described as progressing with age, and the literature notes brow position can change after surgery, sometimes needing separate brow procedures [29][17][20].

claims.claim: Taking out more tissue gives a better result.
claims.believers: Traditional excision-focused approaches assumed that more skin, muscle and fat removed meant a cleaner lid.
claims.experts: Reviews describe a move to conservative, volume-preserving surgery, and a randomised trial found patient-reported scores were similar with or without muscle removal [1][2][24].

claims.believers: Concern about dry eye is common among prospective patients.
claims.experts: A 54-patient randomised trial found subjective dry-eye symptoms improved after surgery and objective tear measures were unchanged at 12 months, while reviews say pre-existing dry eye predicts postoperative problems [23][22].

claims.claim: Surgery changes how others perceive you beyond looking younger.
claims.believers: Patients and surgeons say rejuvenation makes people look more approachable and rested.
claims.experts: A 2015 photograph-rating study of 30 women after facial rejuvenation reported higher rated attractiveness, femininity, likeability and social skills, though the surgeries included more than eyelids [9].

claims.claim: A non-surgical suture or tape can mimic the result.
claims.believers: Taping and glue are widely used to create a crease without surgery.
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes tape and glue create the illusion of a crease; the suture-based approach is covered in a separate entry [28].

card.summary: Removing excess upper-lid skin, muscle and fat through a crease incision; established surgery for hooding, with mostly surgeon-reported evidence.
card.note: Surgical procedure; dry eye and eyelid malposition are recognised concerns.

quick.overview:
Upper blepharoplasty trims loose skin, muscle and sometimes fat from the upper eyelids through an incision hidden in the natural crease. It is done both to clear skin that blocks vision and to reduce a hooded or tired look.

The literature is mostly technique reports and case series, with a few randomised comparisons and an evidence-based review.
quick.mechanism: Redundant tissue is excised along a marked ellipse in the lid crease, and the incision is closed with sutures or tissue glue. It may be paired with brow lifting or ptosis repair [5][7].
quick.risks: Swelling and bruising are common for several weeks [3]. Surgeons screen for dry eye, thyroid eye disease, bleeding disorders and body dysmorphic disorder beforehand [4]. Registered studies are examining dry eye and vision changes after the operation [11][12].

chain: Excess upper-lid skin, muscle and fat removed or repositioned
Lash line and lid crease become visible
Eyes look more open, rested and defined
angle.text: Upper blepharoplasty removes the skin fold that hoods the eye, so more of the eye and the lid crease show. Patients seek it for a more awake, youthful look, and some for improved upper visual field.
